name: Desirial

card.summary: A cross-linked hyaluronic acid injectable made by Laboratoires VIVACY for volume restoration of the labia majora and for vaginal mucosa, aimed at intimate aesthetic and comfort goals.
card.note: Clinician-administered injectable; published data are small, uncontrolled studies.

quick.overview:
Desirial is a brand of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) gel from Laboratoires VIVACY. The Desirial Plus formulation is injected under the skin of the labia majora to restore lost volume, and the original Desirial is injected into the vaginal mucosa.

The appearance payoff is fuller labia majora, which women seeking correction of volume loss or protrusion of the labia minora describe as an aesthetic concern. Two published studies, both small and uncontrolled, report high patient-rated improvement.
quick.how: The gel is injected by a clinician: subcutaneously in the labia majora for volume, or at multiple points in the vaginal mucosa in the pilot study. Outcomes in the studies were collected between 4 weeks and 52 weeks after treatment.
quick.risks: The ESOLANE study reported that Desirial Plus was well tolerated. The vaginal study was a small pilot. Hyaluronic acid fillers generally can cause pain, bruising, redness, and rarely blocked blood vessels or nodules. Reported studies are open-label without a control group.

lead: Desirial is a cross-linked hyaluronic acid product from Laboratoires VIVACY, described as the first cross-linked HA administered by injection in the vaginal mucosa [2]. The Desirial Plus version has been studied as a subcutaneous injection for labia majora volume restoration [1].

The labia majora study was motivated by women who consider atrophy of the labia majora, or protrusion of the labia minora beyond them, aesthetically or sometimes functionally unsatisfactory [1]. Hyaluronic acid itself is a long-established dermal filler used by injection for wrinkles and volume, with effects lasting around six to twelve months in general fillers [4].
Published evidence for Desirial includes an open-label multicenter study of 72 treated women and a 20-patient pilot study, plus a single case report in a foot joint [1][2][3].

chain: Cross-linked hyaluronic acid injected by a clinician
Adds volume to the labia majora, or hydrates vaginal mucosa
Fuller contour and, in studies, reduced dryness and discomfort
angle.text: Desirial Plus is injected to restore volume to the labia majora, changing the contour. In studies, women also reported improvements in comfort and sexual function.

paras: Desirial Plus has been injected subcutaneously into the labia majora in women with hypotrophy or atrophy who request volume restoration [1].
Desirial was studied as multi-point intra-mucosal injections for vulvo-vaginal atrophy, a common consequence of estrogen deficiency after menopause [2].
A 2024 case report describes intra-articular injection of Desirial Plus in a 77-year-old patient with hallux rigidus, with short- and mid-term improvement [3].

The ESOLANE study was a prospective, uncontrolled, open-label multicenter study run between November 2019 and December 2021: 73 women were enrolled and 72 treated with Desirial Plus. At 12 weeks, 97 percent rated themselves improved on the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale, rates stayed above 92 percent through 52 weeks, investigator ratings were above 86 percent, and patients reported better sexual function, fewer symptoms and high satisfaction; the product was reported as well tolerated [1].

A bi-centric pilot of 20 women found no difference in median vaginal mucosal thickness at 8 weeks but significant increases in COL1A1 and COL3A1 gene expression, significantly lower dyspareunia, dryness, itching and chafing, and improved female sexual function scores; 19 of 20 (95 percent) reported some improvement [2].

The ESOLANE investigators describe Desirial Plus as well tolerated [1]. General references on hyaluronic acid fillers list pain, bruising, redness, itching, nerve or microvessel injury, blocked vessels and granulomatous foreign-body reactions as possible complications [4].

timeline.event: Recruitment for the vaginal-mucosa pilot study (19 June 2017 to 5 July 2018) [2].
Case report of Desirial Plus for hallux rigidus [3].
